identity.name: RBZ JEWELLERS LIMITED
identity.industry: Luxury & Consumer Goods / Organized Gold Jewellery Retail & Manufacturing

summary.oneLiner: Revenue and profitability grew strongly on festive demand and retail expansion, with EBITDA margin expanding 63bps QoQ and PAT up 36% YoY; the shift toward higher-margin retail and job work, coupled with strategic store expansion in Gujarat, is redefining the growth trajectory beyond wholesale dependency.

one-line thesis: Revenue and profitability grew strongly on festive demand and retail expansion, with EBITDA margin expanding 63bps QoQ and PAT up 36% YoY; the shift toward higher-margin retail and job work, coupled with strategic store expansion in Gujarat, is redefining the growth trajectory beyond wholesale dependency.
financial scorecard: revenue: +38% YoY (INR190cr); EBITDA/margin: +46% YoY to INR21cr, margin +63bps to 11.19%; PAT (rptd): +36% YoY to INR12cr (6.17% margin); PAT (normalized): ~INR9-10cr (est. excluding INR10-12cr inventory gain); order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR120cr short-term debt, target peak leverage 1:1.2, equity INR300cr
guidance: revenue growth: no formal guidance; margin: no guidance; order inflow: no guidance; capex/commissioning: Surat & Rajkot stores to open in Q2FY27; Gandhinagar & Maninagar mid-format stores planned; no new manufacturing capex planned
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail: INR121cr (+31% YoY); Wholesale: INR67cr (+57% YoY); Job work: INR1cr; B2B total merchandise value: INR843cr; Retail: INR408cr FY26; total B2B+B2C merchandise: INR1,251cr FY26
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 4 stores in Gujarat (Surat, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, Maninagar); potential future entry into other states post-Gujarat dominance; digital campaigns driving daily wear and occasion wear demand
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: Retail ~12-14%, Wholesale ~7-8%, Job work ~6-8%; EBITDA margin improved to 11.19% (Q4) and 14.44% (FY26); cost advantage from in-house manufacturing and 20-25% inventory cushion vs market price
capex / expansion: INR125-150cr inventory required per large-format store (Surat/Rajkot); mid-format stores (Gandhinagar/Maninagar) require lower capex; no manufacturing capex planned; capex funded via debt + inventory transfer + retained earnings
capital allocation: Debt-equity ratio targeted at 1:1 to 1:1.5; no equity dilution planned; profits reinvested into retail expansion and inventory; GML (gold metal loan) being explored for new store funding
risks & watch-items: Gold import duty hike and policy uncertainty; potential black market price arbitrage; consumer sentiment shift post PM's 'don't buy gold' remark; delayed store openings due to market volatility
management quality / tone: Optimistic on long-term growth, conservative on near-term guidance; confident in Gujarat white space; focused on execution, not speculation; transparent on inventory cushion but opaque on exact inventory gains
non-obvious takeaways: Job work revenue decline was due to gold price inflation reducing kg volume, not demand loss — value of merchandise in B2B rose to INR843cr; inventory gain estimated at INR10-12cr, implying normalized PAT of INR9-10cr; retail margins are 3-4% higher than wholesale despite higher opex; 50-55% capacity utilization is sustainable due to gold price inflation doubling revenue without adding artisans

themes.title: Jewellery & wedding-economy formalization
themes.need: Organized jewellery is gaining share via capital-light FOCO expansion and GST/hallmarking formalization, even amid record gold-price volatility. KALYANKJIL posted Q4 revenue +66% YoY with 150 new FY27 stores and a near-zero non-GML-debt target; SENCO/PNGJL/DPABHUSHAN ride regional formalization; SKYGOLD/RGL/GOLDIAM on B2B and lab-grown export; KALAMANDIR on the wedding-wear economy.
themes.driver: Akshaya Tritiya / wedding-season demand; FOCO store rollout; gold-price stabilization lifting volumes.
